title: What College Parenting Is and Why It Matters
summary: The foundations of college parenting: what it is and why getting it right pays off.
body:
Parenting a college student means shifting from manager to consultant: they need emotional support, occasional money guidance, and space to fail safely. FERPA means the college won't tell you their grades.

Why it matters: FERPA blocks parents from grades/records without student consent Most students call home 2-3 times per week freshman year

This guide walks the full ladder — foundations first, then compounded practice, then advanced mastery. Every record is actionable: read in order, do the steps, run the numbers.

title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in College Parenting
summary: Start college parenting this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Set communication expectations before move-in
2. Agree on a budget and how money flows
3. Discuss safety, health insurance, and emergencies
4. Let them solve roommate/professor problems first
5. Visit once in fall - not every weekend

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.
facts: Set communication expectations before move-in
Agree on a budget and how money flows
Discuss safety, health insurance, and emergencies
Let them solve roommate/professor problems first
Visit once in fall - not every weekend

title: College Parenting Beginner FAQ
summary: Straight answers to the most common college parenting questions.
body:
Q: How often should we talk?
A: Let them set the rhythm; 2-3x/week is typical.

Q: What if grades slip?
A: Ask about sleep, friends, and load before grades.

Q: Care packages?
A: Yes - snacks and basics beat expensive gifts.

Still stuck? Start with record 2 of this guide and do the first move today.
